newsitem.title: USA: NGC sees eventual power plant investments.
newsitem.headline: NGC sees eventual power plant investments.

text.p: NGC Corp Chairman Chuck Watson said the Houston company expects to eventually acquire electric generating capacity as utilities begin selling off generating assets in the coming years.

Watson said he expects $100 billion in electric generating assets to change hands in the next two or three years as utilities shed power plants as part of a nationwide restructuring of the domestic electric industry.
"We will be a player in that," Watson said in a speech in Houston. "We'll be building (power plants) or buying them."
Watson earlier had said the Houston company was exploring options for gaining control of generating capacity short of buying stakes in power plants.
Watson said an eventual sell-off of generating assets will pave the way for independent power marketers to gain footholds in electric markets around the country.
"When that happens, I'm convinced it will really open up the market, make it much more liquid," he said.

NGC picked up 350 megawatts enerating capacity and 900 megawatts of demand in its Chevron merger, and its Electric Clearinghouse Inc is the third largest independent power marketer in the fledgling U.S. industry.
